bounds.domain: One managed queue owner, one valid symbolic welcome job, one retained delivery marker and at most two starts. The first row may be pending or abandoned in processing. An imported marker represents an earlier observed provider acknowledgement. A transient outcome replaces one processing row with one pending retry in one storage operation.
bounds.receiptRecovery: A separate projection starts with one processing row and either an observed provider acceptance or a retryable provider failure. Application and acknowledgement are separate. A replay of the same atomic retry after an unknown reply finds the original claim absent and leaves the one pending retry intact. One restart retains the existing storage effects.
bounds.compatibility: One Cloudflare-backed writer, one valid claimed job without a delivered marker and one monotone Worker upgrade. The marker response advertises atomic retry support from the durable state owner. Missing support ends that drain before a provider call and leaves the original processing row. With no pending jobs, the same poller can move the row back and reclaim it after upgrade.
bounds.ownership: GatewayManager starts the queue for the managed Discord bot and joins stop on disconnect. Stop closes new poll admission and joins original recovery and any admitted drain. The test holds an actual successful recovery move reply and, separately, a provider reply while the same owner stops. An admitted drain may finish after stop is requested.
limitations: The model assumes one managed owner and restart from a quiescent or abandoned processing record. It does not establish cross-pod leader fencing, clock deadlines, exact retry counters, marker expiry or provider nonce retention. Enqueue of additional jobs, ordering among several entries, import, invalid payloads and public transport are exercised only by named integration checks where present.

The lifecycle case settles SQLite moves and mutations with their acknowledgements. The receipt-recovery case separates application and acknowledgement for marker writes, processing removal and atomic retry replacement. It assumes the existing authorized Redis commands or a SQLite transaction. A pre-commit failure leaves the original processing row. A lost response after replacement leaves only the delayed retry. Multiple byte-identical legacy processing claims can each match, and old two-step writers can still leave duplicate copies. Both remain outside the single-claim model.

A ready retry may be polled after its backoff. The real tests read the persisted attempt and deadline, restart Workerd and check the same provider nonce on retry. Live Discord delivery, provider deduplication guarantees and arbitrary retries are outside this model. The provider response is controlled in tests while production queue, transport and SQLite operations execute.

Deployment and gateway readiness do not order the Worker and writer. The capability check protects welcome dispatch on a stable older Worker. The compatible protocol must remain available after a successful marker read until that drain settles. Rolling back a Worker during an admitted attempt, mixed-version routing after a valid reply and a perpetually nonempty pending list remain outside the compatibility case.

assumptions: No fairness is required. Stop fences only this queue owner. Work admitted before the stop request may continue until its outcome settles.

No fairness is required. One valid processing row is moved back during startup, removed after a retained marker, replaced atomically with a retry, or dropped after definitive rejection. Storage application and acknowledgement settle together at this projection boundary.

Weak fairness of settle means admitted storage and provider calls eventually return, with the modeled success, rejection or retry outcomes, and local continuations run. Settlement does not imply successful delivery, polling fairness, an elapsed-time deadline or eventual success after retry.

Weak fairness of settle and finishStop requires an admitted recovery or drain to reach its outcome and a fair stop continuation. This includes a rejected startup recovery. Hung external calls and repeated host failures can prevent progress.
No fairness is assumed. An outstanding operation or continuation can stutter forever. The verifier must find a temporal loop.

No fairness is required. A rejected reply leaves the currently committed rows intact. Retry replacement serializes comparison, publication and removal on the selected storage authority. There is no concurrent owner, marker expiry or external deletion.
No fairness is required. One restart reads the same durable storage before marker expiry. The marker derives from an observed successful provider response.
Weak fairness of settleWrite represents a reply or reported failure for admitted writes and their continuations. It does not guarantee successful publication or require a restart.

After one admitted restart, weak fairness of settleRecovery assumes successful storage operations and continuation. It reaches marker replay, no remaining claim, an unconfirmed claim eligible for the same provider nonce, or one retained delayed retry. Further failures, clock progress, repeat sends, Discord deduplication and recovery of legacy duplicate copies remain open.
No fairness is required. A response without the advertised capability is refused even if the state owner has upgraded since it formed that response.

No fairness is required. The authenticated marker-read reply must advertise retry support. Provider dispatch is modeled only after that admission. The supporting Worker does not roll back or route the admitted drain to a legacy state owner.

Weak fairness of advance assumes the same writer continues polling, pending empties, the original claim survives, storage calls and local continuations succeed, and the Worker stays compatible once upgraded. It establishes one provider admission, not provider delivery or an elapsed-time deadline.
